title: Is "brain fry" different for traditional coders vs. vibe coders? (Sharing my weekend family prototype Nemesis Nightware DReam :P  Code name :  Monster Glider)
author: Own_Difference577
selftext:
Hey Reddit,

I'm an amateur vibe coder, and lately I've been wondering whether traditional developers and people like me experience the same kind of creative exhaustion.

I sometimes feel like I'm flying a machine I'm still learning how to build, while experienced developers already understand every bolt holding it together.

Different journeys, different skills, obviously. But when something finally works and a little virtual world comes alive on screen, I wonder how different that feeling really is.

I'm currently experimenting with a small project called **Monster Glider**, under the name *The 3 Wild Monkeys*.

Although, somewhere along the way, a fourth monkey joined the adventure: AI. 🐒

It doesn't magically remove frustration, uncertainty or bad decisions. Sometimes it helps me fly. Sometimes it helps me crash spectacularly. And sometimes we spend hours trying to understand why something that worked yesterday doesn't work anymore.

I also have enormous respect for the people behind tools like Three.js. I jokingly thought I'd buy stock in r/threejs  if I could. Instead, I probably just owe its maintainers a massive thank you.

After getting carried away with an earlier attempt and burning myself out, I'm trying to approach things differently.

My current ambition isn't to build the next big game. It's to create a little world where my family and friends can fly together, explore, get lost and hopefully laugh.

My wife has already contributed to the story for real i stole one of  is "LUMO STORY ;p" , and my family has become my unofficial beta-testing team.

Zero budget. Probably too many ideas. Still learning.

But here's what genuinely interests me:

**Does brain fry affect traditional coders and vibe coders differently? Or, despite our very different approaches, is creative exhaustion something that actually connects us?**

Is the bottleneck writing the code, understanding the code, making hundreds of decisions, or simply caring too much about something you've created?

And how do you keep a passion project alive without letting it consume the passion that started it?

Curious to hear your experiences — including criticism.

Happy coding, however you do it. 🐒

peace (x) Shill

comments.author: funk-it-all
comments.body: Building it so your family and friends can fly around and laugh, instead of chasing the next big game, sounds like a good way to not burn out. Good luck with Monster Glider.

replies.author: Own_Difference577
replies.body: Thanks a ton Mate! Making my family laugh on the weekends is honestly the best metric I could ask for right now. Cheers!  Have a nice one 🙌
